Scholarship overview

Warwick’s AHRC Doctoral Scholarships fund new research projects within the arts and humanities remit. Applicants use the shared Warwick scholarship competition.

Research Areas

  • Arts
  • humanities and related eligible subjects

Funding and duration

ComponentDetails
FundingFull Home/International fees; GBP 5,000 Research Training and Support Grant.
MaintenanceUKRI-rate maintenance stipend
Duration3.5 years

Eligibility and Requirements

Any nationality; a new doctoral project within AHRC’s arts and humanities remit. English evidence, approved equivalents and waivers depend on the programme; IELTS is not a universal requirement for every applicant.

Application dates

ComponentDetails
RecruitmentOpen from 5 October 2026
DeadlineCourse: 7 December; scholarship: 10 December; references: 21 December 2026, all 16:59 GMT

How to Apply

Apply for your doctoral course and the shared Warwick postgraduate research scholarship competition by the separate deadlines.

Warwick advertises up to three AHRC awards within its 2027 competition. Subject coverage extends beyond the available NextApply discipline filters.

About University of Warwick

The University of Warwick offers doctoral study across its faculties and research centres. Its postgraduate research scholarship competition includes several funding streams with a shared application process.

Official details: Programme information

Application route: Application form or official instructions

2026/27 UKRI reference rate: the minimum UKRI doctoral stipend is £21,805 per year, tax-free (London institutions +£2,000), effective 1 October 2026.
